chapters.title: Chapter 1 — Fighting
chapters.text:
At six years old, Ethren Hollowmere was determined to learn how to fight. He was still too small to hold a real sword, but that did not stop him from training with a flimsy wooden one. More than anything, he wanted to prove himself to his father.

Ethren swung at the human-shaped training dummy. Shallow dents covered its sides from years of use, though very few of them belonged to him.

“Ethren! It’s time for breakfast!”

Lucan’s voice carried across the courtyard. His brother leaned out of an open window, wearing the same teasing grin he always seemed to have.

Ethren lowered his sword and hurried toward the manor.

Hollowmere Manor stood three stories tall, built from dark-gray stone. It was large, though nowhere near the size of a duke’s estate. Flower beds filled the courtyard, guards watched the entrance, and warm candlelight glowed behind the windows.

Ethren rushed through the corridors as morning sunlight streamed across the floor. By the time he reached the dining room, sweat clung to his forehead and mud covered his boots.

A long table stood at the center of the room. Alaric, Evelyn, and Lucan were already seated around it.

Lucan smirked as Ethren entered. “Mother, Ethren was training outside again.”

Evelyn’s brows lifted before settling into a concerned frown. “Ethren, what did I tell you about training alone when you can barely hold the sword?”

“But, Mother, I can do it.”

The room fell quiet. A clock ticked above the fireplace while Ethren stared down at his muddy boots.

“I want to be just like Father,” he said, crossing his arms and turning away from her.

Forks and spoons clinked softly against the plates.

Alaric set down his fork. His expression remained calm, though a faint crease appeared between his brows. “Ethren, you are not old enough to train without supervision. You need patience.”

Ethren pressed his lips together but said nothing.

Lucan finished the last of his breakfast and pushed his chair back. “May I be excused?”

Evelyn glanced at the crumbs scattered across his plate. “After you clean up.”

Lucan groaned under his breath.

Alaric turned toward Ethren. “Meet me at the training ground tomorrow before breakfast.”

Ethren’s head snapped up. “Yes, Father,” he replied, struggling to hide his excitement.

After breakfast, Ethren left the dining room and headed toward his bedroom. Lucan’s room stood across the hallway from his own.

A maid followed behind him. “Young Master, would you like to take a bath?”

Ethren looked down at his muddy clothes and boots. His palms were covered in blisters, and even the slightest movement made them sting.

“I probably should, huh?”

Lucan appeared farther down the corridor. He glanced at Ethren, then quickly looked away.

Ethren caught him staring. “Worried about me?”

Lucan blinked and glanced behind himself as though Ethren might have been speaking to someone else.

“Yes, you.” Ethren chuckled.

Lucan folded his arms. “You’re training with Father tomorrow?”

“Yep.” Ethren lifted his chin proudly.

“You can barely hold the sword.”

“Watch me.”

Lucan rolled his eyes, but his gaze dropped to Ethren’s blistered palms. His teasing expression faded for a moment. “You should get those checked.”

Before Ethren could answer, Lucan turned and continued down the corridor.

***

Night settled over Hollowmere Manor. Servants moved through the halls, lighting the wall lamps one by one, while moonlight spilled through the windows.

Inside his office, Alaric sat behind a desk covered in letters and reports. A brass clock hung on the wall above him, its steady ticking filling the room.

The image of Ethren’s blistered palms returned to him.

“Hector, bring me some paper.”

“Yes, Master.”

Hector crossed the office to the bookshelves, retrieved a sheet from a small stack, and placed it on the desk before returning to his place near the door.

Alaric dipped his pen in ink and began to write.

To Doctor Maelin,

I request your presence at Hollowmere Manor at your earliest convenience.

My son, Ethren, has injured his hands while training. The wounds do not appear severe, but several blisters have formed across his palms, and I would prefer that they be examined before they worsen.

Please bring whatever treatment you believe necessary. A carriage will be sent to collect you if required.

Lord Alaric Hollowmere

Count of Hollowmere

chapters.title: Chapter 2 — The First Lesson
chapters.text:
Ethren slowly climbed out of bed. Dark circles rested beneath his eyes; he had barely slept, too excited by the thought of finally training with his father.

Morning sunlight streamed through the window and reflected in his gray eyes. He crossed the room and stopped before the mirror.

His black hair fell messily across his forehead, no matter how often his mother tried to fix it. His eyes were calm in color but unusually observant for a child. Whenever he focused, he tended to stare without blinking, making him appear far more serious than he truly was.

Ethren dressed as quickly as he could and rushed into the corridor, passing several servants along the way.

“Young Master Ethren, slow down!” a maid called after him.

Her words reached him only in fragments. He was already racing toward the courtyard.

Ethren stepped onto the shaded veranda. Stone pillars supported its roof, with short railings connecting them along the edge.

“Father!”

Alaric stood on the sandy training ground with one hand resting thoughtfully against his chin. Four training dummies occupied the yard, which was bordered by the veranda on one side and the manor’s stone walls on the others.

“Ethren, come here.”

Ethren hurried over, struggling to hide his grin. “What are we learning today?”

“We are going to learn how to stand.”

Ethren blinked. “Stand?”

Alaric took a wooden sword and moved into position. One foot rested ahead of the other, his knees bent and his shoulders relaxed. He held the sword firmly in front of him.

“Copy this stance.”

‘Standing sounds boring,’ Ethren thought. Still, if his father considered it important, he would do it.

He took a wooden sword from the rack and copied Alaric’s position, gripping the handle with both hands.

Alaric’s expression remained controlled, but a brief spark of pride appeared in his eyes. “Not bad. This is a proper stance—the foundation of swordsmanship.”

Ethren straightened slightly.

“Now hold it until I tell you to stop.”

Ethren remained in position. At first, it seemed easy. Then his arms began to ache, and his legs trembled beneath him.

A minute passed.

His vision blurred.

Then came the ticking.

Louder.

Closer.

For a moment, the training ground vanished.

An enormous clock hung in a dark, empty world. Its single hand turned backward with a slow, grinding motion. Cracks spread across its face before the entire clock split apart.

Behind it stood a faceless creature covered in unfamiliar markings. Smaller clocks hovered around its body, each one turning at a different speed.

Ethren’s knees buckled.

Alaric caught him before he struck the ground. For the first time that morning, worry broke through his controlled expression.

“Are you all right, Ethren?”

Ethren forced a smile. “Yeah, I’m fine. It was nothing.”

Alaric studied him for several seconds. “That is enough. You pushed yourself too far.”

“But—”

“You will rest.” His voice left no room for argument. “We can continue once you have recovered.”

Ethren reluctantly sat beneath the veranda.

During the break, a knight crossed the training ground and stopped beside a crack in the manor wall. A brown, translucent crystal about the length of his forearm appeared beside him. Thin bronze rings revolved around it, their surfaces etched with glowing symbols, while several stone fragments orbited its core. The knight pressed his palm against the damaged wall.

The broken pieces shifted. Dust fell from the crack as the wall sealed itself, leaving no sign that it had ever been damaged.

Ethren leaned forward in awe. “Father, what was that?”

“A Vestige.”

“What’s a Vestige?”

“A Vestige gives its bearer power over a Principle,” Alaric explained. “Most appear as floating crystals, but their color, markings, and surrounding rings change according to their Principle and bearer.”

“That’s so cool! Where’s yours, Father?”

Alaric rested a hand on Ethren’s head. His expression became guarded.

“That is none of your concern.”

Ethren frowned. Why did Father refuse to tell him? It had to be something important.

After resting, Ethren returned to the training ground. Alaric kept the remaining exercises short and forced him to take several breaks, but Ethren continued until the afternoon light began to fade.

At last, Alaric lowered the wooden sword. “That is enough for today.”

“No, not yet!”

“You can barely keep your eyes open.”

Ethren opened his mouth to argue, but a yawn escaped instead.

Alaric placed a hand on his shoulder and guided him back toward the manor.

***

Alaric’s Office

Later that evening, Alaric entered his office and sat behind his desk. A sealed letter rested among the reports waiting for him.

He broke the wax and began to read.

To Lord Alaric Hollowmere, Count of Hollowmere,

House Rosenthal extends its respects to you and your household.

After careful consideration of the future interests of both our families, I have determined that a formal union between House Rosenthal and House Hollowmere would benefit the stability and prosperity of our territories.

My daughter, Lady Celestine Rosenthal, has reached an appropriate age for an engagement to be established. Your son, Ethren Hollowmere, possesses a respectable name, suitable upbringing, and a position worthy of consideration.

Therefore, I propose that Lady Celestine Rosenthal and Ethren Hollowmere be formally betrothed.

The engagement would strengthen the relationship between our houses, secure cooperation between our territories, and ensure that both families benefit from shared political and economic interests.

Representatives of House Rosenthal will arrive at Hollowmere Manor on the fifteenth day of the coming month to discuss the formal conditions of the arrangement.

I trust that House Hollowmere understands the importance of this opportunity and will respond accordingly.

Marquis Severin Rosenthal

Head of House Rosenthal

chapters.title: Chapter 3 — The Arrangement
chapters.text:
Silver moonlight streamed through the windows of Alaric’s office. The room was neat and orderly, warmed by the quiet fire burning in the hearth.

“Dear, this arrangement could hurt Ethren,” Evelyn said.

“What are we supposed to do? If we don't accept this, our house—” Alaric’s voice tightened.

“No,” Evelyn said softly but firmly. “Our family.”

***

The next morning, Ethren found his parents waiting for him at the dining table.

Ethren entered the familiar dining room, where the fireplace cast a warm glow across the long table. Alaric turned towards him, “Ethren, sit. We have something to tell you.”

Ethren glanced at the table and saw Lucan making a grinning face. Ethren sat right next to Lucan.

“What’s happening?” Ethren whispered.

“No clue.” Lucan leaned closer, still grinning, “But looks like you're in trouble.”

After Ethren sat down, he picked up his fork and started eating. Plates of freshly baked bread, sausages, and eggs were spread across the table. Usually, Lucan would be talking up a storm ,but this morning everyone sat unusually still.

“Ethren, we received a message from Marquis Rosenthal,” Alaric said calmly. “Ethren, you're getting engaged to Celestine Rosenthal.”

Ethren thought Lucan would laugh or at least say something, but he just stared at Alaric with a blank expression.

“What?” Ethren exclaimed, lowering his fork.

Evelyn turned toward Ethren. “This engagement could help you meet other noble children and make friends outside our family.”

Ethren’s gaze shifted to his mother. Can’t I make friends without marrying someone? Ethren's gaze dropped, his earlier excitement disappearing.

Alaric’s back straightened, and glanced at Lucan. “Lucan, you will start to train with Ethren today.”

Lucan immediately stood, clenched one fist, and pressed it against his chest in a salute.

“Yes Father, I was getting bored of just watching Ethren anyway.”

A proud smile began to form on Evelyn’s lips, but later showed a serious expression. “Lucan.” Evelyn warned, though her expression remained calm, “Remember, your attire is in the wardrobe.”

Lucan turned his head towards Ethren’s direction and he smirked.

“Yes, Mother.”

Lucan pushed his chair back, stood, and slid it back into place before heading for the door. Ethren rushed to the door, following Lucan. Ethren trailed behind Lucan staring at his back with his formal black attire.

Lucan glanced back at Ethren, “Heard that Ethren? I'm gonna train with you.”

Ethren met Lucan’s gaze and lifted his chin.

“Watch me, I'm gonna beat you.”

***

The Training Ground

Lucan and Ethren stood on the training ground practicing the same stance Ethren learned. Ethren’s legs started shaking.

“Your stance is slipping,” Lucan said with a grin.

“You think?” Ethren replied dryly.

“You two, focus,” Alaric ordered.

The engagement still bothered him, but the thought of finally training with Lucan pushed it aside.

“Line up,” Alaric said.

Ethren stood face-to-face with Lucan, a confident grin on his face. The sand beneath them was uneven from years of training. The wooden dummies stood along the edge of the yard while Alaric watched nearby.

“Begin,” Alaric ordered.

Lucan dashed forward and struck Ethren’s shoulder with a dull thud. Ethren staggered backwards, struggling to decide on what to do.

What? How is Lucan so fast?

“Hey, I'm right here,” Lucan taunted from beside him. Lucan darted to Ethren’s right and struck him across the back with a sharp smack. Ethren fell face-first into the sand.

Lucan laughed, “Eating dirt, I see?”

Ethren immediately got up and swung his sword at Lucan’s throat. Lucan blocked his strike with a thud. Ethren dashed backwards, his breath was ringing in his ears. He looked up and met Lucan’s gaze, he was always trailing behind Lucan, always struggling to catch up. Now, he couldn’t even land a single hit. Ethren gripped his sword and his brows lowered and lunged at Lucan.

“Whoa, angry much?” Lucan asked, surprise entering his voice.

Lucan sidestepped the attack, leaving Ethren to fall into the sand.

“Too slow, brother.” Lucan said while pointing his sword at Ethren’s back on the floor.

“Enough,” Alaric shouted, his brows furrowed, “Lucan, stop antagonizing your brother.”

“And Ethren, control your anger. The moment you stopped thinking, you lost.”

“Sorry Father,” Lucan replied, offering Ethren his hand.

Ethren slapped Lucan’s and picked himself up. The sound of clapping filled the training ground. Captain Cedric Pole stepped away from the gathered knights and approached the brothers. He had earned his position years ago after saving Alaric from a monster, becoming one of the few men the count trusted completely.

Cedric pole walked towards the brothers, still applauding.

“Good job boy’s,” Cedric said with a broad smile, “Alaric, your boys have talent.”

“Yes, but they have much to learn,” Alaric replied, his gaze settling on the brothers.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 — Physician
chapters.text:
Lucan walked through the shadowed corridor. Only thin strips of moonlight slipped past the curtains. Statues lined the walls between those windows. Eventually, he stopped at Ethren’s door.

While getting dressed for bed, Ethren noticed Lucan enter. Once Lucan entered he headed to the bed and sat.

Ethren tried several times to pull on his nightgown, but his trembling arms refused to cooperate. Each attempt made him groan and grimace.

“What do you want now, Lucan?” Ethren groaned.

Lucan gave him a gentle smile. “Only to talk to you.” After a brief pause, Lucan spoke, “I just wanted to ask if you're okay.”

Ethren pouted. “Yeah I’m fine.”

“Glad to hear it,” Lucan replied. He stood up from the bed, approached Ethren and pulled him in for a hug. He rested one hand on Ethren’s head, gently patting his hair.

Ethren pushed him away. “Get away from me, weirdo.”

“All right, fine,” Lucan replied, ruffling up Ethren's hair.

Lucan headed towards the door and slowly opened it. Glancing back, Lucan waved at Ethren, and Ethren waved back.

***

Ethren’s Bedroom

Ethren woke up to the sound of footsteps rushing through the hallway. The servants rushed to begin their duties. Ethren got up to dress himself. Before he could finish, the door creaked open and a butler came through.

“Young Master, a physician has arrived to check on you,” the butler said.

“All right,” Ethren replied, still trying to pull on his shirt.

A man of average build entered through the door. He stood nearly as tall as Alaric, but slightly shorter. He wore an oversized white coat reaching his knees, gloves covering his hands with a leather case on his right. Round spectacles rested on the bridge of his nose.

The man wore a gentle smile. “Ah, you must be Ethren.”

‘This must be the physician, who else could it be.’

By the time the man entered, Ethren had put on his clothes.

“Yes, that would be me,” Ethren replied.

The man looked around and spotted a chair and gestured toward it.

“Ethren, please sit here,” the physician said.

Ethren walked towards the chair and sat where the physician had directed. The man pulled over a second chair and sat across from him, placing the leather case beside his chair.

“Now,” the physician said gently, holding one gloved hand, “let me see your palms.”

Ethren slowly placed his hand on the man's gloved palm. Maelin readjusted his glasses and leaned closer, staring at Ethren’s palm.

“My name is Maelin,” the man said.

“My name is Ethren,” Ethren replied.

“I know that,” Maelin said with a quiet laugh.

A stone appeared beside Maelin, its surface covered in symbols Ethren could not understand. The stone shone with a bright blue color and the same glow had spread across Maelin’s hand. Water formed around his fingers and spiraled gently over his glove.

A gentle warmth spread through Ethren’s hand.

‘Whoa, this is a Vestige—but why is it blue?’

The knight’s Vestige had possessed a brown glow. Maelin’s Vestige looked completely different. He couldn’t hide his excitement. His eyes brightened, and a smile spread across his face.

“What is that?” Ethren asked.

“Ha, this is a Vestige,” Maelin explained.

Ethren pouted. “I know that, but what does your Vestige do?”

Maelin leaned closer, pretending to look stern. “Why should I tell you, boy?”

Ethren put on his best puppy-dog face, "Pleeease?"

“All right, fine,” Maelin responded, his brows resting in a soft expression. “Vestiges are manifestations of Principles. Each Vestige is unique to its bearer. Their abilities vary, but always remain connected to their Principle.”

After a brief pause, Maelin glanced at his Vestige. “For example, Ethren, mine is called the ‘Vestige of the Gentle Current.’ Its Principle is Water. It can move, create, and control water. However, my Vestige specializes in healing, so the water I create can only be used to examine injuries and heal them.”

“That’s so cool,” Ethren exclaimed, leaning in closer.

‘When will I get mine?’

***

That evening, the Hollowmere family gathered in the dining room.

The room’s curtains were half closed so moonlight slipped past. The fireplace crackled nearby, and the forks clinked softly against the plates, while quiet chewing filled the room.

Evelyn faced toward the two brothers. “How was training, you two?”

“It was—” Ethren began.

“He tripped over his own boot,” Lucan said, covering his mouth to hide his grin.

Ethren’s cheeks turned red, and he glared at Lucan.

Ethren glanced at his father. “Father, I wanna learn about Vestiges.”

“Of course,” Alaric replied, turning to Lucan, “You will be learning Vestiges as well, I will arrange a tutor to teach both of you.”

***

That night, Ethren had a dream.

A dream without end. A peaceful village stretched before him. Farmers tended their fields, neighbors gathered outside, and children chased one another. All things moved toward an ending, whether they wished to or not. In the center of that dream, Ethren saw a boy walking through the village with a happy expression. The dream blurred, when it became clear, the village burned. The boy turned into a knight clad within a steel plate, with his visor lowered covering his face. The dream shifted again, and the knight turned old. Wrinkles covered his weathered face, and beneath one eye rested a scar shaped like an unfamiliar symbol.

The village had been rebuilt. At the center, an old man sat on a bench. Kids gathered around the old man. He read them a story about a noble who had their life stolen from them. He sought revenge so he scoured the entire world searching for who had done this to him and slaughtered them.

Suddenly, the old man stared at Ethren.

Ethren had no words. What was he supposed to do?

“Hello?” Ethren called out.

‘There no way he’ll respond.’

The dream froze

The world fell still

For a moment, time itself seemed to stop.

The old man gave a faint smile, with his eyes closed. “Hello.”

The dream ended.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 — The Fading Hour
chapters.text:
Ethren jolted awake. He sat up quickly and pressed a hand against his aching head. The dream had been strange, but that was not what disturbed him most. The old man had spoken directly to him. What had that story even meant?

‘How did he respond to me?’

‘Well, it was my dream after all. Maybe I made it up. Yeah, that must be it.’

Ethren tried to dismiss it as a nightmare, but the old man’s words remained clear in his memory.

A door creaked open, and a butler stepped inside.

“Sir, House Rosenthal has come to visit.”

“All right, let me get dressed.”

***

Reception Room

Ethren was dressed simply, though still formally enough to receive noble guests.

Ethren sat with Alaric on a small two-seater sofa. Across from them were Celestine and her father. Celestine had glossy blue hair and equally blue eyes, making her immediately noticeable. She resembled her father in the shape of her face and her sharp gaze. Although faint wrinkles lined his face, he had the broad shoulders of a well-built knight.

‘Father has a better physique,’ Ethren thought proudly.

“What is the purpose of your visit, Marquis?” Alaric asked.

Marquis Rosenthal crossed his legs and stared at Alaric with a thin smile.

“Just to go over the terms of our children's engagement.”

Alaric looked toward Ethren with a stern expression.

“Ethren, show Lady Celestine around the manor,” Alaric instructed.

Marquis Rosenthal gestured for Celestine to follow Ethren.

Ethren approached the door, opened it, and held it for Celestine.

Celestine smiled and stepped out. Ethren’s face flushed bright red. He had never spent time alone with a girl his age before. He was really excited to have a friend to talk to.

Ethren stepped out and guided Celestine toward the dining room. Since he had never had a friend his age, he struggled to think of what to say.

Celestine noticed Ethren staring at the floor.

“Hey, I'm right here. What are you looking at?”

Ethren glanced at Celestine and quickly turned away. His face flushed again and he placed his hand on his head.

“Oh, uh, hello.”

Celestine looked at Ethren.

“Hello,” Celestine said shyly.

Ethren turned toward Celestine. Her eyes were more beautiful up close, and her smile was radiant.

A few moments later, they reached the dining room, and Ethren opened the door.

He smiled. “Here is where I eat with my family.”

Celestine entered the room and looked around. The room was massive, and one could fit a training ground here.

“Wow, this is big,” Celestine exclaimed.

Ethren smiled.

“Yup.”

Celestine approached the window and looked outside. Sunlight fell across her face. Her expression was calm, though something about it seemed troubled. The window overlooked the training ground, where Cedric Pole led several knights through their exercises.

‘Why can’t I stop staring at her?’ Ethren thought.

Celestine pointed toward the training ground. “Hey, can we go there?”

“Sure, let me lead you there.”

Later, they reached the veranda. Ethren spotted a bench and gestured for Celestine to sit. The bench faced the training ground, and he assumed that Celestine wanted to watch the knights train. Celestine took a seat, and he sat beside her.

After a long silence, Celestine spoke up.

“What are your thoughts on our engagement?”

“I haven’t thought much about it,” Ethren admitted. “But I trust my father.”

After a brief pause, Ethren smiled at Celestine. “I trust my whole family.”

Celestine smiled back and returned to watching the knights.

It was peaceful. Ethren wished he could have more moments like this. A gentle breeze swept his hair across his face. Perhaps engagements were not as bad as he had thought.

***

Study Room

After bidding farewell to Celestine, Ethren had his first lesson on Vestiges.

Ethren was excited to learn about Vestiges, while Lucan seemed bored. That didn’t bother him.

A broad-shouldered man stepped through the doorway, carrying several books beneath one arm. He stood around the same height as Evelyn and had neatly combed dark-brown hair.

Ethren and Lucan were already sitting at a desk, so the man pulled up a chair and sat next to Ethren.

“You must be Ethren,” the man said.

The man smiled and placed his books on the desk.

“My name is Harold.”

Harold waved at Lucan since he was sitting farther away, but Lucan didn’t notice because he was staring at the floor.

Harold stood and walked over to Lucan.

“Young Master Lucan,” Harold whispered into his ear.

Lucan jolted and straightened his back. He slowly turned to his right and noticed Harold smiling, the corners of his eyes lifted with amusement.

“Hello?”

“Hello, Sir Lucan.”

Ethren stared at Lucan and started giggling.

Lucan noticed and glared at him.

Harold returned to Ethren’s desk, grabbed two books, and set one in front of each boy.

“Read these,” Harold instructed. “If you have any questions, ask me.”

Twenty minutes later, Ethren finished his book. He turned to his left and found Lucan slumped over his desk, looking ready to give up.

Ethren’s book explained the known Vestige ranks. According to it, six ranks had been officially recorded, numbered from Rank 0 to Rank 5.

Rank 0, Bearer, began when a person awakened their Vestige. At Rank 1, Inscribed, a mark appeared somewhere on the bearer’s body, representing their growing connection with their Vestige.

Rank 2, Forged, strengthened the bearer’s body and increased their resistance to dangerous dimensions. At Rank 3, Unsealed, the bearer’s appearance began changing to reflect the nature of their Vestige.

The book offered no explanation of the two ranks beyond Unsealed. It listed only their names: Regnant and Eidolon.

Eidolon. Ethren read the unfamiliar word. He wondered why the book offered no explanation. He decided to ask Harold.

“Harold, why does the book not explain Eidolon or Regnant?”

Harold was about to scold Lucan when he heard Ethren.

“Knowledge of the higher ranks is restricted,” Harold explained. “Even most tutors are forbidden from studying them.”

Lucan lifted his head and turned toward Ethren. “You haven’t even awakened your Vestige, so it isn’t something you should worry about, Ethren.”

“Go back to reading, Sir Lucan,” Harold scolded.

Lucan pouted and picked up his book. “Fine.”

“Can I get another book, Teacher?” Ethren asked.

“Of course,” Harold replied.

Harold picked up another book and set it down near Ethren.

Ethren picked up the book and stared at its cover.

The title on the cover read Vestige Principles.

Ethren quickly opened it and began reading. He had always wondered which Principle his Vestige might possess.

As Ethren neared the end of the book, he realized that several pages had been torn out. Before he could ask Harold about them, the book began to tremble in his hands.

When he looked again, the missing pages had returned, as though time had reversed. Astonished but too curious to call for Harold, Ethren began reading the first restored page.

The passage read:

“The Principle of Time:

Records recovered from ancient Dimensions describe its harrowing power. No recorded Vestige has ever possessed this Principle.

Several brave Eidolons entered a Dimension known as The Fading Hour, a world shaped by the Principle of Time. Within it, they discovered shrines and temples dedicated to an unknown bearer of that power.

He exists only in the outcome—but was he also the beginning? No one knows where or when he came from. When the last surviving Eidolon attempted to escape the Dimension, he simply disappeared.”

Ethren turned to his right. “Teacher, look at what it says in this book!”

Harold was getting ready to pack up when Ethren spoke to him. Harold bent down to look at the book.

When Ethren glanced back, the passage had disappeared as if it had never existed. The page remained, but it was completely blank.

“Ethren, I think you’re getting tired. It is already dark, and I believe you need some sleep.”

Ethren glanced toward the window. Darkness had swallowed the training ground. Hadn’t sunlight filled the room only moments ago?

‘Could I have made it up?’

chapters.title: Chapter 6 — The Valemont Banquet
chapters.text:
Four years later

Today was Leander Valemont’s birthday, and Ethren’s family had decided to attend his banquet.

Over the past four years, Ethren had learned a lot. He had learned how to use a sword and how Vestiges worked. He had also studied noble houses, important figures, and powerful people. Now, he had finally turned eleven—the age when children awakened their Vestiges and became Bearers.

A short while later, the Hollowmere family’s carriage departed for the Valemont estate.

***

Inside the Carriage

Ethren looked out the window, waiting for them to arrive. Alaric and Evelyn were talking, while Lucan slept.

The carriage was quite comfortable, and the seat was warm and soft. Ethren could feel it shake over the uneven ground. The sound of birds chirping filled his ears, and the ride felt peaceful.

Outside the window, sunlight shone over a nearby lake. Ethren watched the scenery to pass the time. His eyes eventually grew heavy and began closing on their own. Before long, he fell asleep against the window.

Someone shook him awake. Ethren slowly opened his eyes and saw Lucan in front of him, holding his shoulders.

“What do you want, Lucan?” Ethren asked groggily.

Lucan smiled and looked out the window.

Ethren turned toward the window. A massive manor filled his view, though he still could not see the entire structure. Hooves clopped outside, and he could tell that many other carriages had arrived.

Lucan stepped out onto the pavement.

Ethren noticed Alaric and Evelyn already outside talking to another noble.

He got up and stepped out of the carriage.

The man his parents had been speaking with walked away, and Alaric and Evelyn approached Ethren.

“Ethren, you finally woke up,” Evelyn said with a smile.

Ethren returned a smile. “Who was that man?”

“That was Lord Valemont, Leander’s father,” Alaric replied.

Lucan shrugged. “Who cares, let’s go in.”

Evelyn gave Lucan a cold stare, then turned toward the manor.

Evelyn and Alaric started walking toward the manor.

Ethren trailed behind them.

A few minutes later, the Hollowmere family entered the banquet hall.

An extravagant chandelier hung above countless guests. Hanging pots filled with flowers lined the walls, adding to the comfortable atmosphere. Tables covered with food were spread across the room, while a group of people gathered in one area to play chess.

Ethren noticed a group of noble children gathered nearby. That was when he spotted Celestine. Her blue hair stood out among the other nobles, so he recognized her immediately. Several children around Ethren’s age surrounded her.

Ethren said goodbye to his parents and Lucan and walked up to Celestine and her group.

Celestine’s eyes briefly met Ethren’s before she quickly turned back toward the group.

‘She saw me, right?’

As he continued toward the group, a boy seemed to notice him.

A boy with pure-white hair stood among the guests, his strands nearly dazzling beneath the light. His defined jaw and sharp nose gave him a cold, striking appearance.

“Hey, whatever your name is, I don’t recommend talking to them,” the boy said, glancing toward Celestine’s group.

“But hey, don’t worry about them. My name is Cassiel. What about you?”

Ethren stared at him, caught off guard by the boy’s sudden introduction.

“My name is Ethren,” Ethren said, snapping back to reality.

“Why should I not talk to them?”

“They are just a bunch of entitled rich brats,” Cassiel replied, smiling.

Ethren stared at the group. Celestine was speaking to a boy who looked slightly older than him. He stood with effortless confidence, dressed in a finely tailored black-and-gold coat. A relaxed smile rested on his face as he spoke, and the other children seemed to gather around him naturally, as though he expected to be the center of attention.

“Who’s that guy talking to Celestine?” Ethren asked.

Cassiel wrinkled his nose in mock disgust and glanced toward the group.

“Oh, Leander. He’s the most entitled brat you can find here.”

Cassiel saw Ethren staring at Celestine.

“What’s your deal with Celestine, anyway?” Cassiel asked as he leaned closer to Ethren with a grin.

“You keep staring at her, it’s giving me stalker vibes.”

Ethren rubbed the back of his neck and avoided Cassiel’s gaze.

“She’s my fiancée.”

Cassiel gave him a sympathetic look. “Oh, crap. That sucks.”

Ethren glared at Cassiel and quickly replied.

“What’s wrong with her?”

“Well, first off, she’s the worst. She’s rude, mean, and... well, rude. Those are the only words I can use to describe her. She may seem like an angel toward adults, but don’t be fooled. She insults me and bullies me.”

Ethren didn’t know how to react. Was she really this bad?

“Sorry to say it, buddy, but I don’t think Celestine even likes you. She and Leander are stuck together like glue. They’re always together.”

“Don’t even get me started on the others, especially my sister,” Cassiel said.

A tight feeling settled in Ethren’s chest, but he refused to believe Cassiel without speaking to her himself.

“Well, I’m gonna see for myself whether you’re right or not,” Ethren said, forcing confidence into his voice.

Ethren walked up to the group of nobles his age. They were gathered in a lounge area with two couches, laughing and talking.

He counted five people in the group. One of the girls sitting on the sofa had bright red hair and wore a beautiful dress covered in jewels. She wore an arrogant smile, as though she believed herself better than everyone else.

A broad-shouldered boy stood quietly near the edge of the group. His short brown hair was neatly combed, and his steady hazel eyes moved carefully across the room. Unlike the others, he did not appear interested in drawing attention to himself.

As Ethren finally reached Celestine, his face reddened. He placed a hand behind his head.

“Hey, Celestine.”

Celestine turned toward him with an indifferent expression.

“Greetings.”

She returned to talking to Leander, but Leander seemed to notice Ethren.

“Who’s this guy?” Leander said, looking at Ethren.

The entire group followed Leander’s gaze and stared at Ethren.

The brunette girl remained seated, watching him without sharing the others’ surprise. Her hair was arranged into a neat bun, and her pale skin caught the chandelier’s light. Rather than staring, she studied Ethren with a calm, measuring gaze, as though deciding whether he was worth remembering.

“Mirelle, are you going to keep staring at him?” the red-haired girl asked.

“I’m observing,” she replied without looking away.

Celestine blushed and stared at the floor.

Ethren gave a confident smile to Leander.

“My name is Ethren Hollowmere.”

“Ethren Hollowmere?” Leander’s eyes flicked briefly toward Celestine. “So you’re—”

“Hey, Leander.” A tall-framed boy with bright blond hair approached him.

Leander quickly turned toward the voice.

“What do you want, Prince Evander?”

“Still hiding behind your birthday guests?” Evander asked with a smug smile. “You avoided our last match. I want a rematch.”

Leander’s relaxed smile vanished. From the way they glared at one another, Ethren could tell this was not their first confrontation.

The brown-haired boy tried to break them up, but to no avail.

“Leander, it’s not worth it. Just back off.”

Leander grinned. “Let’s take this outside.”

chapters.title: Chapter 7 — Realization
chapters.text:
The Valemont training ground stood in front of Ethren. It was way bigger than his own training ground. He kinda wished his was this big. Footprints from the knights who trained there covered the sand, while a thin layer of dust drifted across the field. The sun was starting to set, casting a warm glow over the grounds. Trees surrounded the field, their leaves shifting as a light breeze swept through them.

A massive number of nobles gathered around the grounds, standing along the stone path that led toward it.

Whispers filled Ethren’s ears.

“Is that the crown prince…”

A noble quickly responded, “It is. Look at his platinum-white hair.”

Ethren stared toward the training ground, where Leandor and the crown prince stood.

Leandor pulled off his black cape and let it fall to the ground, revealing a white linen shirt beneath.

Ethren could tell they were trying to flaunt their physiques.

The crown prince responded with a grin and did the same.

They glared at each other face-to-face, neither willing to back down.

A couple of girls standing next to Ethren squealed and gawked at the crown prince.

Ethren couldn’t help but feel a hint of jealousy. He had always admired his brother for being handsome, and a tiny part of him wanted that attention too. So when the crown prince received the same attention, his jealousy only grew.

Suddenly, Ethren felt a tap on his shoulder.

“Hey, Ethren, what’s going on?” Lucan asked.

Ethren quickly turned around, startled.

He redirected his gaze toward the two nobles on the field. “I’m not too sure myself. The crown prince suddenly came up to him and asked for a fight.”

“Ah, they’ve always had a history. Crown Prince Evander would always pick a fight.”

“Celestine spends most of her time with them now,” Lucan said.

Ethren’s gaze drifted toward her. She stood nearby with Mirelle, Rowan, and Seraphina.

They didn’t stand too far away from Leandor and Evander. Celestine clasped her hands together, Rowan watched with a tense jaw, and Seraphina barely glanced at them.

Ethren glared at Lucan. “I know.”

Lucan grinned. “What’s with the cold shoulder?”

He smiled and gestured toward a stone slab for them to sit on.

“Anyway, enjoy the fight.”

Ethren wondered where his parents were. He surveyed the area again, but couldn’t find them.

Still no sign of them.

Suddenly, the training ground became quiet. Only scattered whispers remained.

The knights guarding the entrance to the field tensed, and Ethren stared at the man who had just entered.

He had a lean figure that highlighted his soft features. His blond hair swayed in the breeze, and his deep-set ruby eyes surveyed the area. He wore a black leather coat over a white linen shirt. A belt rested around his hips, and his black trousers were slightly wrinkled.

He made his way toward Leandor and leaned toward his ear.

The man seemed to be instructing Leandor. Ethren was curious about what he was saying, but it wasn’t his problem.

The man turned toward the crowd with a bright smile.

“Hello, everyone. My name is Derick Valemont, the father of Leandor.”

He gestured toward his son before redirecting his gaze toward Evander.

“Crown Prince Evander has asked my son for a duel.”

“I will be judging this fight, so everyone sit back and watch the might of the Valemont family.”

The field erupted with applause. Some questioned whether he was disrespecting the royal family with that statement, while others gossiped about who was stronger. Ethren was excited for the match. Across the empire, these two were said to be among the most promising young nobles.

Once the applause stopped, Derick Valemont looked toward the two boys.

“The rules are simple. You are only to stop once the other is unable to continue. The use of Vestiges is allowed.”

“Use any means necessary to win.”

With that, he started the countdown.

The fight began.

Leandor immediately dashed forward and thrust his sword toward Evander’s chest.

Evander caught Leandor’s sword with his left hand, the tip barely touching his chest.

Gasps and cheers filled the training ground. Even Lucan’s eyes widened.

Lucan quickly regained his composure and wore an approving smile.

“Impressive.”

Evander held a sly grin and swung his sword toward Leandor’s neck at an impressive speed.

In that split second, Leandor stared at the blade coming toward his neck and barely ducked beneath it.

Ethren couldn’t believe it. If he had been in Leandor’s position, the fight would’ve already been over.

Suddenly, the air beside Leandor began to shake.

It seemed as if the space beside him was about to break.

When silence filled the training ground, it appeared.

A yellow crystal floated beside Leandor.

Its golden glow shone across the field. Runes covered its surface beneath a translucent layer that resembled ice, while its aura spread throughout the entire area.

If Ethren had to describe it, it looked like a crystal encased in ice.

The cheering grew louder. Shouts and screams filled the training ground. Some of the older nobles finally showed interest, their gazes settling on Leandor with knowing smiles.

Ethren knew awakening a Vestige at Leandor’s age wasn’t unusual for those fortunate enough to possess one. Still, his desire to awaken his own only grew.

He had to be patient.

A dark bruise had already spread across Evander’s left palm from catching Leandor’s sword. Instead of backing away from the newly manifested Vestige, his grin widened.

“Not bad at all, Leandor.”

Evander lunged forward, sweeping his blade toward Leandor’s knee.

Leandor twisted his lower body to the right. The blade passed by his knee, but the sudden movement left him in an awkward position.

Leandor’s Vestige began to glow.

Its golden shine took form around him, hardening into a translucent barrier. Even the sand seemed to pull away from its surface as if nothing could pass through it.

To Ethren, it seemed impenetrable.

Evander took his chance while Leandor was still off-balance and swung his sword against the barrier.

Clang!

The barrier remained completely unbroken.

“Ha! You thought that would break my barrier?” Leandor mocked.

“Tch.”

Evander’s face darkened, losing its bright confidence.

Thud.

Leandor’s sword hit the ground.

His face filled with confusion.

His arms wouldn’t move. He couldn’t feel them. It was as if something had reached inside him and pulled the strength straight from his limbs.

Then a strange, screeching sensation tore through his chest. His heartbeat quickened. His breathing shortened. His head spun as he desperately tried to understand what was happening to him.

He slowly looked up.

Evander was staring back at him.

And then Leandor finally understood the feeling.

Fear.
